criteria.quote: Magnemite floats, but iron can come flying.
criteria.revision: Open with the measured claim and the unresolved pairing: “Magnemite’s side units keep it airborne—and draw iron objects from over 300 feet away. How?”

criteria.quote: Magnemite’s side units keep it airborne while drawing iron objects from over 300 feet away.
criteria.revision: Replace the broad “keep it airborne” phrasing with the researched mechanism: “Its side units emit electromagnetic waves that let it float, while their magnetism draws iron objects from over 300 feet away.”

criteria.quote: How can Magnemite float and still pull distant iron?
criteria.revision: Make the question harder to answer by withholding the shared mechanism until later: “Are Magnemite’s floating and its long-range pull really separate abilities?”

criteria.quote: That pull reaches iron objects more than three hundred feet away.
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated distance beat with a new consequence from the research: “But when its internal electrical supply runs out, Magnemite becomes incapable of flight.” Then connect that fact to its electricity dependence.

Delay the distance reveal until after explaining that the side units keep Magnemite airborne, then reveal: “Those same units can draw iron objects from over 300 feet away.” The contrast makes the existing fact feel more surprising without strengthening it.

criteria.quote: The same side units that keep it airborne generate powerful magnetism.
criteria.revision: Cut the later repetition, “The units do two jobs at once,” and use that scene for a distinct fact: “Magnemite feeds on electricity—and can end up grounded when its supply is depleted.”

criteria.quote: Magnemite’s side units solve two problems at once: staying airborne and drawing in iron.
criteria.revision: Make the ending resolve the mechanism and add the researched limitation: “Its side units keep it aloft with electromagnetic waves, yet their magnetism reaches iron over 300 feet away. Run out of electricity, and Magnemite loses flight.”

criteria.quote: Clever two-job design, or too much magnetic power?
criteria.revision: Use a split grounded in two explicit research claims: “Which is more unsettling: Magnemite drawing iron from over 300 feet away, or being a frequent cause of power outages?”
